title: docs(audits): pre-deploy audit 2026-10-15 — feature map, findings, report and fix plans
body:
## Update 2026-10-26 — 11 plans shipped, ready to merge

Eleven plans have shipped since this PR opened: 02, 04, 05, 07, 19, 28, 29, 31, 32, 35 and 36 ([#358](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/358)–[#360](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/360), [#367](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/367)–[#374](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/374)). Their PRs could not delete them, because the plans lived only on this branch. Commit `2ec09233` deletes them here.

- `plans/audit-2026-10-15/00-index.md` drops their rows. It gains a **Shipped** table (plan, findings closed, PR), so the "every finding appears exactly once" coverage claim stays checkable. Batch 4 now reads "All shipped".
- The index and report status banners now say 11 of 36 plans shipped, 25 open.
- SHOT-B2 (plan 05) did not ship. [#360](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/360) dropped it because its premise no longer holds on `main`. The Shipped table says so.

Commit `494208bd` fixes the nine notes the agent review left on the open plans and the report. Six of them were defects a plan executor would have copied: a flaky test in 08, orphan tags in 17, a test in 21 that passed without the fix, a 2 s heartbeat gap in 25, and a resubscribe on every render in 27. Each thread has a "Fixed in" reply.

**Why merge now:** once the plans live on `main`, each fix PR deletes its own plan and index row. That is the rule the index states, and it ends this manual cleanup on every batch.

**Checks for this update** (at `494208bd`): pre-push `verify-local` → 24/24 tasks successful; `bun run build` in `apps/documentation` → exit 0, 330 pages built. Grepping `dist/` for links to any of the 11 deleted plan slugs → 0 files. `oxfmt --check apps/documentation` → clean. The branch merges into `main` without conflicts; GitHub reports `CLEAN`.

**Verify it yourself:** `cd apps/documentation && bun run dev` and open `/plans/audit-2026-10-15/00-index/`.
- Expect 25 plan links and an 11-row Shipped table whose PR links open merged PRs.
- Broken if a Shipped row still links to a plan page, or a plan page that exists has no row.

---

Adds a periodic **pre-deploy audit** to the docs site, records its first run against `main` at `d36b19dd`, and — in the second half of this PR — adds **one implementation plan per root cause** covering every finding. This is documentation only: no app code changes.

## Part 1 — the audit

Three steps:

1. Four read-only agents (Sonnet) mapped the four core features — record, screenshot, library and edit video — covering files, flows, IPC and hot paths.
2. Eight read-only auditors (Opus) reviewed them, two per feature. Lens A covered performance and observability; lens B covered errors, bugs and logic.
3. The orchestrator consolidated the results and re-verified the highest-impact findings by hand.

**Outcome:** 78 raw findings (0 critical, 6 high, 49 medium, 23 low), about 68 distinct after merging overlaps.

The main slowdown traces to **Library re-list churn**. Every Library, detail and Editor-home mount fires a cloud-catalog refresh. That refresh always broadcasts `library:changed`, which costs about 4 full vault scans per navigation. On the detail page the second list flips `isLoading`, so the video player unmounts and restarts.

The 6 high findings: four silent data-loss paths (REC-B6, VID-A1, LIB-B1, and the shared write races), one trim-handle bug a user hits on first use (VID-B1), and the Library churn (LIB-A1, LIB-A2).

## Part 2 — the fix plans

`plans/audit-2026-10-15/` holds an index plus **36 plans**, one per root cause, grouped in the report's six batches (measure first → data loss → Library fan-out → trim → recording failure paths → render/copy cost). Every one of the 78 finding IDs appears in exactly one plan's `Closes:` line (checked by script, 0 duplicates). Each plan was written from a Sonnet analysis of the current code and follows the writing-plans format: goal, architecture, constraints, review focus, then bite-sized TDD tasks with the actual test and implementation code, the commands to run, and the PR's "How to test it yourself". Plans are working documents: the PR that ships one deletes it.

New pages:
- `/audits/` — the method page and the log of runs.
- `/audits/2026-10-15/feature-map/`, `/audits/2026-10-15/report/`, `/audits/2026-10-15/findings/*` (8 pages).
- `/plans/audit-2026-10-15/00-index/` and `01-…` through `36-…`.

## What to review

1. **`apps/documentation/src/content/docs/plans/audit-2026-10-15/00-index.md` — the finding → plan mapping and batch order.** Decide whether the batch order (measure first, then data loss, then Library) is the order you want to execute, and whether any plan should be split or dropped.
2. **`apps/documentation/src/content/docs/audits/2026-10-15/report.md:21` — the ranked "why it feels slower" list.** It was derived from code and micro-benchmarks, not from profiling the running app. Plan 01 (telemetry) exists so the next audit can be measured.
3. **Plans with cross-plan ordering notes in their Global Constraints** — 02/08/22 (recording writer), 04/06/09 (atomic writes), 10/12/13 (`library-service.ts`), 20/23/24 (`recorder-engine.ts`), 27/03 (editor loader), 33/34 (`png-size`). Decide whether to execute them in the stated order or merge neighbours into one PR.
4. **`report.md:63` — the caveats.** Only LIB-A1, LIB-A2, REC-B6 and VID-B1 were re-verified by the orchestrator; every plan's code is written against the analyses, not run. The first task of each plan is a failing test, which is what catches a plan that is wrong.
5. **`apps/documentation/astro.config.mjs:64` — the new top-level "Audits" sidebar group** (autogenerated from `audits/`; `/audits/` already serves static files from `public/audits/` and the build confirms no collision).

**Safe to skim:** `findings/*.md` are the auditors' raw output with frontmatter added. `feature-map.md` is reference material. Within each plan, the test code blocks restate the "Review Focus" list above them.

## Checks

- `astro build` (apps/documentation) → exit 0, 316 pages built. A script checked every `/audits/`, `/backlog/` and `/plans/` link in the new pages against `dist/` and found 0 missing.
- A script extracted every `Closes:` ID across the 36 plans → 78 distinct IDs, 0 duplicates.
- `pre-push verify-local` (turbo: types, lint, tests across the monorepo) → 24/24 tasks successful on every push.
  - The first push attempt (part 1) failed in `kaipu-record#check-types`; the cause was a stale `node_modules` in the audit worktree (mediabunny 1.49.0 installed vs 1.61.4 in the lockfile). `bun install --frozen-lockfile` fixed it; the lockfile was not touched.

## Manual verification

- [ ] `cd apps/documentation && bun run dev`, open `/plans/audit-2026-10-15/00-index/`. Expect 25 plan links plus the Shipped table, each link opening a page whose "Closes:" line matches the index row, and the report's status banner linking back to the index.
- [ ] To confirm the main finding (LIB-A2) in the app, open a recording's detail page while signed in and play the video. Expect a brief "Loading" flash about a second after opening, after which the player restarts.
- [ ] To confirm VID-B1, open a recording in the video editor and drag the **left** trim handle of a clip slowly to the right by a few pixels. Expect the trim to race far ahead of the pointer.

## What I did not verify

- I did not run or profile the app, so every magnitude in the report is an estimate from code reading or out-of-app micro-benchmarks.
- No plan's code was executed. Each plan's tests were written to fail on today's code and pass after the change, but that is by reading, not by running. Expect selector names, helper names and a few line numbers to need adjusting when a plan is executed; the plans say so where the analyst flagged it.
- The recording auditors checked mediabunny behaviour against 1.49.0 (the worktree's stale install), not 1.61.4. REC-A1, REC-A6 and REC-A7 (plans 20, 24, 25) should be re-checked; plans 20 and 29 did verify against 1.61.4.
- Linear tickets exist now (created after this PR was opened): batch parents NIW2-381 → NIW2-386, one sub-issue per plan NIW2-387 → NIW2-422, chained with blocking relations so the queue respects the batch order and the shared-file groups.
